If you are a resident of Shelby County, Tennessee, or have business dealings in the county, chances are you have heard of the Shelby County Circuit Court. Understanding the Shelby County Circuit Court

The Shelby County Circuit Court is one of the largest and busiest trial courts in Tennessee. The court is a part of the 30th Judicial District of Tennessee and is located in Memphis, Tennessee. The court handles a wide range of civil and criminal cases and has a significant impact on the lives of people living in Shelby County. The court has a staff of judges, attorneys, and administrative staff who work tirelessly to ensure justice for all.

History of the Shelby County Circuit Court

The Shelby County Circuit Court has a long and rich history dating back to the early 1800s. The court was established by the Tennessee Constitution of 1834 and has undergone significant changes since then. The court has played a critical role in shaping the state's legal system and has been instrumental in upholding the rule of law.

Jurisdiction of the Shelby County Circuit Court

The Shelby County Circuit Court has broad jurisdiction and is responsible for handling civil and criminal cases. The court has jurisdiction over cases involving more than $25,000 in damages, felony criminal cases, and a range of other legal disputes. The court also handles cases involving child custody, divorce, and probate matters. In addition, the court has a special division dedicated to handling cases involving drug offenses and mental health issues.

Services offered by the Shelby County Circuit Court

The Shelby County Circuit Court offers a range of services to the public, including access to court records, mediation services, and legal resources. The court also has a dedicated self-help center that provides assistance to people representing themselves in court. The court's website provides a wealth of information and resources, including forms, rules, and court calendars.

Structure of the Shelby County Circuit Court

The Shelby County Circuit Court is divided into several divisions, including civil, criminal, family, and probate divisions. Each division has its judges and staff responsible for handling cases in that area of law. The court is presided over by a chief judge who oversees the operations of the court and ensures that cases are processed efficiently and fairly.
